newsitem.title: UK: EMERGING MKT RISK MIXED IF US STOCKS FALL - FLEMINGS.
newsitem.headline: EMERGING MKT RISK MIXED IF US STOCKS FALL - FLEMINGS.

text.p: Argentina, Hong Kong, Venezuela, Poland and Mexico are the emerging markets most at risk from a correction in U.S. equities, Robert Fleming and Co said in a research report.

Flemings' Global Emerging Markets research team said in a report published on Monday it used two methods to assess which markets would be most vulnerable to a correction in US equity markets this year and said the five appeared in the top ten most at risk in both studies.
"These may be underweighted by investors who are concerned at the prospect of a U.S. equity market correction," the report by Jonathan Garner and Alexander Holcroft said.
It said Slovakia, Botswana, Mauritius, Ghana and India were least at risk from a correction in the S&P 500 and should be overweighted in a defensive portfolio.
The team used two methods to rank 36 emerging markets and the five countries it identified as most and least at risk showed up as such in the top ten of both studies.
The first method ranks the markets by under-performance in 1994 and outperformance in the 12 months to end-January 1997.
That table found the 10 most vulnerable markets were Turkey, Poland, China, Venezuela, the Czech Republic, Argentina, Hong Kong, Mexico, Hungary and Zimbabwe.
The least vulnerable were Korea, Mauritius, Slovakia, Kenya, South Africa, Chile, Peru, Botswana, India and Thailand.
The second model studies the markets' sensitivity to returns in the S&P500, using an econometric study examining factors influencing dollar returns over the last three years.

The markets whose returns were most closely correlated with the S&P500, and so vulnerable to a correction, were Brazil, Argentina, Hong Kong, Venezuela, Poland, Mexico, Israel, Peru, Thailand and Chile.
The lowest correlations were found in Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Jordan, Sri Lanka, Botswana, China and Ghana.
The report said a continuation of the "Goldilocks" economy in the U.S. this year, with moderate GDP and employment growth, should generate steady gains in the U.S. equity market.
But many market players say that higher U.S. rates or falls in corporate profitability could lead to a sizeable correction in the U.S. equity market.
